newsitem.title: JAPAN: Profile of Japan's embattled state nuclear firm.
newsitem.headline: Profile of Japan's embattled state nuclear firm.

text.p: Here is a profile of the Japanese nuclear firm which has been accused of a series of cover-ups concerning accidents at its facilities.

Established as a state-run public corporation in 1967, the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC) carries out research and operates nuclear plants, aiming to recycle nuclear material and help Japan achieve energy self-sufficiency through nuclear power.
The corporation employs 2,820 people and its annual budget, provided from government funds, stands at 234.6 billion yen ($1.87 billion).
Four of its six main facilities have now been shut down following accidents.
Major facilities:
-- Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor Monju
Located near Tsuruga on the Sea of Japan coast, 350 km (220 miles) west of Tokyo. The reactor, called Monju, is designed to produce more nuclear fuel than it consumes.
Monju reached criticality -- the point at which a nuclear reaction begins -- in 1994 but was shut down in December 1995 after a massive coolant leak.

The PNC has admitted covering up details of the way the accident was handled and trying to suppress video tape of the site after the coolant leak. A Monju public relations official committed suicide over the affair.
-- Advanced Thermal Reactor Fugen.

Located near Monju, the reactor uses heavy water and is the world's first reactor to burn uranium and plutonium mixed-oxide (MOX) fuel. The theory is that spent fuel from the reactor, named Fugen, can easily be reprocessed to be used again.

The Fugen reactor has been in operation since 1978 but it was shut down on Tuesday after a leak of tritium exposed 11 workers to radiation. The PNC said there had been 11 other radiation leakage accidents at Fugen since November 1994.
-- Tokai Reprocessing Plant:

Located at Tokaimura, 100 km (65 miles) northeast of Tokyo, the reprocessing plant produces plutonium by recycling spent nuclear fuel. It handles 12 percent of Japan's total spent fuel, with the rest reprocessed at plants in France.
An explosion at the plant's bituminisation facility, where low-level waste is mixed with asphalt for permanent storage, on March 11 exposed 37 workers to small doses of radiation.
The PNC shut down the plant after the accident. It later admitted it had lied about safety procedures in a report about the explosion and police are now investigating the case.
-- Plutonium Fuel Development Plant

Located near the Tokai Reprocessing Plant, this facility is designed to produce fuel for Fugen and Monju. This has been shut down since March 17 when an alarm signalling that the plant was at critical mass -- the point at which a nuclear reaction becomes self-sustaining -- went off as a result of a malfunction.
-- Experimental Fast Breeder Reactor Joyo
Joyo, an experimental fast-breeder reactor, went into operation in 1977 and is located near the Tokai Reprocessing Plant.
-- Uranium Enrichment Plant

The PNC's predecessor, the Atomic Fuel Corporation, started uranium mining operations in Ningyo-toge in Okayama, western Japan, in 1956. The plant enriches natural uranium to make fissionable uranium. The PNC also runs plants carrying out research into advanced forms of uranium enrichment.
